https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/16/four.text: Three children and one teacher were shot dead at an elementary school in the northwestern US state of Oregon on Thursday, police said, adding that the assailant was a 16-year-old who was killed by an armed bystander.Another child and a teacher were being treated for critical injuries after the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary school in Bend, a city of about 100,000 people.Mike Krantz, police chief of Bend, told journalists that the department first learned of an active shooter after a call from a person who reported being shot at multiple times by a person carrying a long gun.Dozens of emergency calls then reported that a shooter had entered the school and all law enforcement in the area were called to the scene, Krantz said.Officers arrived at 1:02 pm local time (2202 CET) within minutes of the calls, said the police chief."Moments later, an officer reported that the suspect had been shot by a community member who had seen the suspect enter the school and pursued him into the school and engaged him," Krantz continued."Our officers entered the building and confirmed the suspect was dead."Officers performed emergency aid on the victims. The three children who died on the scene were aged five, eight and 11, the police chief said.One teacher was also pronounced dead.Krantz said one seven-year-old and one 54-year-old teacher with critical injuries were transported by medics to a local hospital.He added that the shooter was a resident of Bend.Krantz stressed that the investigation was in its early stages, but told a press conference it appeared "the shooter had forced their way into the school by shooting at locked doors."'Unthinkable tragedy'Between 400 and 450 children attend Silver Rail Elementary, where more than 40 staff work, a police spokesperson had said earlier.After a lockdown, Bend-La Pine School District said law enforcement was escorting students in buses to a separate location, where families could reunite with their children.The district's superintendent, Steve Cook, tearfully called the day's events "an unthinkable tragedy.""We are heartbroken. We are horrified. This is the kind of thing you hear about in other places, and pray that it never happens here," he told reporters.Parents were anxiously waiting at the site near a church, where parent Drew Sharp told CBS News: "I have faith that he's okay and that he'll be alright."Sharp said his son was a fifth grader, the highest grade in the school, and that children were disembarking from the bus youngest to oldest."Which makes sense," Sharp said, but "it's just more time waiting."Friday classes at schools across the district along with activities and athletic events were canceled, Bend-La Pine said in a statement.The elementary school is approximately 270 kilometres southeast of the city Portland. It serves primary-age students in kindergarten through fifth grade.'Cannot keep accepting this'The United States, where firearms are readily available, is a frequent scene of gun violence, with thousands of people killed every year. It has the highest rate of gun-related deaths among all developed nations.The deadliest school shooting in US history took place at Virginia Tech on 16 April 2007, when South Korean student Seung-Hui Cho killed 32 people and wounded 17 others before taking his own life.There have been more than 360 mass shootings in the US so far this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as four or more people shot."Our hearts are with the terrified children and the families anxiously waiting to hear that their loved ones are safe," GIFFORDS, a gun safety organisation, said on X."We cannot keep accepting this as a fact of life."Thursday's shooting was followed by a painfully familiar chorus of calls for action on gun control, pleas that have resulted in little meaningful change.In the face of decades of massacres akin to Thursday's, the powerful US pro-gun lobby has given millions of dollars to primarily conservative politicians in a successful bid to keep gun laws loose."They're killing our babies. Shredding our kids with lead. Forcing us to live in fear," said Janelle Bynum, an Oregon congresswoman, in a statement."This continues to happen," she said later, speaking on CNN."And it seems as if the adults don't care."

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq62.text: Image source, Christoph Greztmacher Image caption, Eva Greztmacher, 76, had spent many years in Niger as an aid worker By Basillioh Rukanga Published 22 October 2026, 09:21 BST Updated 36 minutes ago Two women - a Swiss and an Austrian â have been freed after more than a year in captivity in Niger and handed over to authorities in the Libyan city of Benghazi. Austrian national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss Claudia Abbt, 69, were kidnapped separately in the northern Nigerien city of Agadez in January and April last year. No details have been given about who was holding them or their demands, although some reports have previously linked the kidnapping to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of their release were not disclosed. Libyan officials were reported as saying the women would be handed over to authorities in their respective countries after necessary procedures were completed. Libya's al-Masar TV showed the two women entering what looks like an ambulance and later being attended to by a health worker. Speaking in French, the women thanked Khalifa Haftar, military commander of eastern Libya, and his son, Saddam Haftar, for their release. Gretzmacher was an aid worker who had lived for many years in Niger, while Abbt had spent several years living and working as a community worker in Agadez. A plane was expected to leave Benghazi on Thursday, first stopping in Vienna to transfer Gretzmacher to Austrian authorities before continuing to Switzerland with Abbt, privately owned Air Info Agadez news outlet reported. Libya has struggled to recover from the chaos that followed the 2011 Nato-backed uprising that toppled long-time ruler Muammar Gaddafi. It is split between two administrations - one in the east backed by Haftar, and the other in the west in the capital Tripoli, led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah. Under Gaddafi, many ethnic Tuaregs from Mali and Niger were recruited to join armed groups loyal to him in Libya. After he was killed, many went home. Analysts say this has been a major factor in the spread of instability in the Sahel region. Niger and its neighbours have faced years of jihadist violence, including kidnappings and deadly attacks, carried out by different groups linked to al-Qaeda and Islamic State. The country has been under military control since 2023 when Gen Abdourahmane Tchiani deposed the country's elected President, Mohamed Bazoum. https://www.politico.eu/article/wes-stre.text: BERLIN — German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius will host his British counterpart Wes Streeting in Berlin on Monday, Nov. 2, for talks on NATO, Ukraine and bilateral defense cooperation, Germany's defense ministry announced Wednesday. Streeting, who took over as Britain's defense secretary in July, will make his inaugural visit to Berlin in his new role as part of the German-British Defence Ministerial Council. The two ministers will meet at the defense ministry's headquarters, where Streeting will be received with military honors before laying a wreath at the Bundeswehr memorial. Advertisement Advertisement According to the ministry, discussions will focus on the international security situation, the two countries' contributions to NATO, military support for Ukraine and closer defense-industrial cooperation. The visit comes as Berlin and London seek to deepen their defense partnership under the landmark Trinity House Agreement signed in October 2024 and the broader Kensington Treaty concluded in 2025. The meeting follows an E5 gathering of Europe's five major defense powers — Germany, Britain, France, Italy and Poland — in Paris on Monday, where ministers pledged to assume greater responsibility for European security while maintaining close cooperation with Washington.
